findings_to_judge.finding: Edge Retail Academy's US independent-jeweler panel shows the category decelerating sharply in August 2026 — gross sales +5% YoY (vs +18% in June and +10% in July), units -8%, average retail sale +14% — with the opening-price-point sterling silver / alternative metals category at -5% dollars and -19% units; August is month one of Signet's fiscal Q3 and the month the H2 guide has to be built on.

The 15% Section 122 global import surcharge that underpinned Signet's 'mid-teens effective tariff rate for the year' expired 12:01am on 2026-07-24 and was replaced the same minute by Section 301 forced-labor duties of 10%–12.5% on the 60 economies covering Signet's sourcing base — a 2.5–5 point step down on India, the country Signet named as its principal tariff exposure, four days before its quarter ended and seven weeks after the FY27 guide was set.

Signet has filed IEEPA refund claims on most goods where it was importer of record and had received only 'a small amount' as of 2026-06-02, with management stating it is too early to quantify the amount or timing 'as well as how any proceeds may be used' — meaning the FY27 guide contains none of it, while CBP had already built out mass electronic IEEPA refunds covering ~82% of affected entries by April 2026, i.e. during Signet's Q2.
